meta.boot: the vanilla CoreServer asset pipeline: Options.parse([]) for the option set, an inert HytaleServer/Universe stub (event bus without listeners, universe without players) and the vanilla AssetRegistryLoader static initializer, which registers every vanilla asset store with its path, codec and load order
meta.moduleStores: the vanilla server registers a few more asset stores from its plugin modules (UnarmedInteractions, Interaction, RootInteraction, HitboxCollisionConfig, RepulsionConfig, MovementConfig, EntityStatType, PatternedConnectedBlockRuleSetAsset and CustomConnectedBlockTemplateAsset); they are registered here with the verbatim vanilla definitions (without the packet generators, which would drag in the client protocol)
meta.codecVariants: the vanilla server registers the codec variants of its plugins in the plugin setup (the fluid tickers, the benches, the connected block rule sets and shapes, the block tick procedures, the farming stages, the falling block impacts and the knockbacks); they are registered here with the verbatim vanilla definitions, because without them the corresponding BlockType and Fluid fields cannot be decoded
meta.loadOrder: the pack is mounted as a zip FileSystem (java.nio.file.FileSystems.newFileSystem) exactly like the vanilla server; the asset files of every store are collected with Files.walkFileTree (the vanilla mechanism) and loaded in that order, so the ids follow the zip entry order of the pack. The dumper runs with a single worker thread of the common fork join pool (-Djava.util.concurrent.ForkJoinPool.common.parallelism=1), because the vanilla pipeline decodes the assets in parallel and collects the results in a ConcurrentHashMap whose iteration order would otherwise depend on the thread scheduling
meta.idOrder: ids are handed out by BlockTypeAssetMap.putAll0 / IndexedLookupTableAssetMap.putAll0 in asset-load order: the four pre-loaded block types (Empty, Unknown, Debug_Cube, Debug_Model) come first (ids 0-3), then the standalone block assets of Server/Item/Block/Blocks and finally the block types embedded in the Server/Item/Items item assets
meta.idOrderCaveat: the ids are pinned to the load order observed by this dumper. They are only identical to a real server's ids when the real server loads the same pack in the same order; compare against a real-server dump before relying on the ids.
meta.commonAssets: the pack's CommonAssetsIndex.hashes is read into the static CommonAssetRegistry so that the CommonAssetValidator accepts the texture / model references of the item assets
meta.packetGenerators: the vanilla packet generators are registered but never run: the universe stub has no players, so no packet is produced
meta.blockTypeSource: the block type definitions are the "BlockType" objects embedded in the Server/Item/Items item assets; Item.CODEC registers them as child assets of the BlockType store via ContainedAssetCodec (mode INHERIT_ID_AND_PARENT), so the block id equals the item key and the parent chain is inherited from the item's "Parent"
meta.deterministic: no timestamps are written; the dump is byte-identical across runs
meta.knownGaps: the prefab list assets (Server/PrefabList) cannot be decoded because they reference the prefab store, which the dumper does not boot; the single block type that references such a list (ExamplePrefabPlacementBlock_Tree) is therefore missing from the registry. The asset stores the registries do not depend on (the interaction, particle and weather stores) also report load failures for the same reason - they do not influence the block, fluid and environment ids.
